issues.legal_issue: An appeal that abates for failure to substitute a deceased respondent is not disposed of by a decree on the merits, and a second appeal cannot be brought against the abatement as though such a decree existed.
material_facts: A respondent died while a first appeal was pending, and no substitution was made within the prescribed time.
The first appellate court held that the appeal had abated but also stated that it was dismissed on contest and a decree was drawn up in those terms.
The first appellate court had not adjudicated the parties’ rights on the merits.
issues.conclusion: The first appeal stood disposed of by abatement, not by a decree; the purported decree dismissing it on contest was contrary to law and non-existent, so no second appeal lay against it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a decree requires a formal adjudication conclusively determining rights. Order 22 Rules 4, 9 and 11 govern substitution and abatement; abatement occurs by operation of law and is not an adjudication on the merits. Section 100 permits a second appeal from a decree passed in appeal, not from an order refusing to set aside abatement. The provision barring a fresh suit after abatement also reflects that abatement is not an adjudication attracting res judicata under Section 11.

predicates.first_appellate_proceeding: The proceeding was an appeal before a court hearing an appeal from the trial court.
predicates.appeal_abated_for_non_substitution: A respondent died during the appeal and the required substitution was not made within the prescribed time.
predicates.no_merits_adjudication: The appellate court disposed of the proceeding because of abatement without deciding the parties’ rights on the merits.

issues.definition: When an appeal abates for non-substitution without a merits adjudication, no decree arises and a second appeal cannot be brought as though a decree had been passed.

issues.legal_issue: The dismissal of an incompetent second appeal does not render an independently competent appeal from an order refusing to set aside abatement infructuous.
material_facts: The first appellate court refused to set aside abatement and substitution after finding insufficient cause for the delay.
The appellants brought an appeal from that order, which the High Court allowed after finding sufficient cause, setting aside abatement and permitting substitution.
A separate second appeal was dismissed, although it was incompetent because no decree had been passed in the first appeal.
The High Court Division Bench treated the dismissal of the second appeal as making the appeal from order infructuous and set aside the order allowing it.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal of the incompetent second appeal did not affect the competent appeal from order or the decision allowing it; the Division Bench’s decision was set aside and the Single Judge’s decision was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Order 22 Rule 9(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure permits an application to set aside abatement on proof of sufficient cause, and an order refusing that relief is appealable under Order 43 Rule 1(k). An incompetent second appeal cannot affect the merits or validity of a competent appeal from an order. The Court also noted, without deciding, that a Letters Patent appeal would not lie from a decision in an appeal under Order 43 Rule 1.

rule.if: appeal_from_order_proceeding and order_refused_to_set_aside_abatement and second_appeal_was_incompetent and second_appeal_was_dismissed and appeal_from_order_allowed_after_sufficient_cause_found

predicates.appeal_from_order_proceeding: The proceeding was an appeal from an order concerning abatement.
predicates.order_refused_to_set_aside_abatement: The lower court refused to set aside the abatement of an appeal.
predicates.second_appeal_was_incompetent: A party brought a second appeal despite there being no decree from which a second appeal could lie.
predicates.second_appeal_was_dismissed: The court dismissed that second appeal.
predicates.appeal_from_order_allowed_after_sufficie: The court hearing the appeal from the order found sufficient cause for the delay, set aside abatement and allowed substitution.

issues.definition: When a competent appeal from an order setting aside abatement has been allowed, dismissal of an incompetent second appeal does not make that appeal from the order ineffective.
